#4096. Grand Theft Auto VI Review - Outrageous Fortune

Many superlatives will be heard in the discussion around Grand Theft Auto VI – biggest world, most activities, best graphics, deepest narrative – but its real triumph is the way all those features and others work in service of a cohesive, believable immersion in a criminal fantasy that is hard to grasp until you’ve played it for yourself.

Rockstar’s latest returns players to a dramatically expanded version of the Vice City seen in a prior game, now largely unrecognizable after real and in-game years have passed. Leonida is a joy to explore, filled with a wealth of activities, both mundane and illicit. The game’s design makes many ordinary tasks as compelling as the illegal ones. Go fishing off the boat, brew coffee to wake up, work out at the gym, scuba dive for long-lost treasure, dust crops, motocross in the mud, go dancing at the club. As you move between those activities, the world feels alive with minor events, from traffic accidents to shady individuals a little too interested in your walk to the ATM. GTAVI delights in life's minutiae, with animations, voice lines, and background characters that keep things fresh even dozens of hours into the story. The level of detail everywhere is astounding and, at times, overwhelming. Getting sidetracked is easy.

The focus on detail carries into the visuals. Lucia’s hair blows in the wind, and she absently pushes it back behind her ear. A drug den is littered with paraphernalia and empty containers. A shifty contact quirks a smile – your only hint that things are about to go south. Sweat glistens on your character’s skin after a hard workout, their breathing and heart rate noticeably heightened. Clouds roll together in the sky, creating realistic weather simulations. The commitment to an authentic simulated world is encompassing, thoughtful, and intentional, a testament to hand-crafted and meticulously painstaking development work, paying off in an absorbing play-space that is hard to step away from.

While the day-to-day simulation is fascinating, it also adds pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward. Not even one of these meticulously choreographed sequences deserves to be spoiled; they run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect.

Ranged combat is punchy and enjoyable; smart use of cover and time-slowing focus makes most battles manageable. On-foot navigation is in a similar boat – simple to pick up and uninterested in needless complexity or challenge; the focus is on choosing smart moments for stealth, knowing when to run and when to fight, and selecting the precise instant for a burst of sudden action. Driving is fast and intense, made more appealing by a huge variety of functionally distinct vehicles to enjoy. If there’s a fault to the core and optional story missions, it’s that many feel a bit on rails regarding where to go and what to do at each step. At the same time, that directed approach keeps the pace relentless, and the action and outcomes thrilling. Over many hours, the game morphs and throws new wrenches into the mix at key junctures, teasing and then playing out criminal experiences from petty theft to group heists to illicit spec ops, and punctuates those distinct vibes with memorable and singular moments.

Like its predecessors, GTAVI simultaneously lampoons and celebrates life in modern America, taking aim at targets like social media, wellness lifestyles, rap and music culture, manosphere content, and dozens more. The caricatures land so well because, in many cases, they’re (sadly) barely over the line of the absurdity we see reflected in real life, and because Rockstar so ably captures individual subcultures, dialects, and situations. Behind it all is a scathing critique of wealth inequality and the inherent unfairness of a system that sets most up to fail. It’s a bitter message delivered in honey-wrapped, exhilarating gameplay, but it shines through.

Of all its significant feats, the relationship between Lucia and Jason elevates the game to new heights, lending this installment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries. This is, without a doubt, video gaming’s most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you’re left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts. The two collectively suffer the slings and arrows of a world that always seems stacked against them; the fortune they amass is not a power grab, but a desperate attempt to cling to each other and come out the other side together, and the player can’t help but cheer them on and dread how fate might stand in the way.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.

Alex Van Aken contributed to this article.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4093. GodLike Esports sweep Trigger Point Esports to stay unbeaten in South Asia Kickoff qualifier

GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier. Only two South Asian sides will reach the Last Chance Qualifier, where a single place at Kickoff in Bangkok is on offer.

GodLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

The playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

GodLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

GodLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

South Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

The qualifier also has a new organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not said why it made the change.

The UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

GodLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

#4092. GTA 6: How to Find the Secret Satan Boss

Christian Bognar is a Contributor at DualShockers with over three years of experience covering the gaming industry. Since 2022, he has written guides and reviews for publications including DualShockers, CBR, Attack of the Fanboy, PC Invasion, and The Game Slayer. He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration

GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida. Some examples include the Kraken deep underwater, UFOs, and even a Mario and Luigi reference.

One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight. Not only is it a really trippy mission, but it also rewards the player with one of the best weapons in the game.

A conspiracy theorist, a waffle house and a toxic sewage chamber – here's how to finish The Final Flush in GTA 6 for a permanent stamina boost.

If you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the secret Satan boss fight in GTA 6.

To find the secret Satan boss in GTA 6, you must travel to the northern side of Port Gellhorn and visit the house with “Welcome to the Hellhole!” written on it. You can find the exact location of this house in the image of Port Gellhorn below.

When you arrive at this house, the garage will either be open or closed. The Satan boss fight event can only be triggered if the garage is open, so if it happens to be shut when you arrive, then you’ll have to come back another time. This event all comes down to RNG, but there are ways to increase your chances.

A new Grand Theft Auto 6 Easter Egg has been discovered that involves the player being trapped in a horrific Squid Game-style horror event.

First, the garage has a higher chance of being open late at night. For example, it was open for me around 10:00 PM, so I recommend only visiting the Hellhole house around this time.

Keep in mind that the event won’t trigger if you just wait outside the house. Instead, I recommend using the RydeMe app to fast travel to another location and back to the house multiple times until the garage opens. This worked for me after five attempts.

Once the garage finally opens, walk inside to find two men having some drinks. They will ask you if you want a beer, which you should grab from the cooler next to the couch.

For the next couple of minutes, make sure you don’t do anything to piss these guys off. You can talk to them, but don’t choose the “provoke” dialogue option or throw a bottle to mess up the event. Instead, wait patiently until their van arrives.

A new Grand Theft Auto 6 Easter Egg has been discovered, where a random NPC has seemingly discovered the game's biggest secret.

When the van arrives, the men will ask you to join them for their upcoming ritual. You should agree here and climb into the back of the van, which will then transport you to another location with a bonfire.

Next, get out of the van and make your way to the bonfire to celebrate with the two Satanists, and wait until they tell you to look into the fire. Once the prompt “look into the fire” pops up, hold down the button to do just that.

Looking into the fire will teleport you to hell, where you’ll have to fight a wave of Satan’s demons and Satan himself.

Satan is not very difficult to defeat, but the fight can be a bit confusing. What you want to do here is shoot the exploding enemies that are running toward you, which will turn Satan’s health bar red.

This is a brief guide that entails the location of the Fast and Furious green Eclipse in GTA 6.

Once the health bar is red, you want to shoot at Satan to drain his health. When the health bar turns back to black, you want to repeat the process and kill the surrounding enemies to turn the bar red again.

Doing this a few times will have Satan going down fairly quickly. Once you kill Satan, you will teleport back to the real world.

When players respawn back to the real world after fighting Satan in GTA 6, they will be granted a permanent health increase. Additionally, they’ll be able to claim the Hellspawn Cumshot 12 Shotgun next to the large throne.

This shotgun is extremely powerful and is one of the best guns I have found in the game so far, so I recommend equipping it for any upcoming missions you have.

The world of Grand Theft Auto is connected, and there are many connections between GTA 5 and the latest game in the series.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4089. Escape From Tarkov Trades Halloween for New Graphics Engine in Latest Update

Halloween has ended, making way for jollier celebrations and bigger gifts. In the communal spirit of Thanksgiving week, which is absolutely not a thing in Russia, Escape from Tarkov has dropped one of its biggest updates since its 1.0 launch last year.

Patch 1.3.5.0 for Escape From Tarkov marks the end of its traditional Halloween event, which means Scav violence is back to its normal levels.

The highlight of the update is on the performance side, where Battlestate Games has unlocked improved frames across the board, thanks in part to an engine upgrade that finally brings Escape From Tarkov to current-gen standards.

One of the biggest complaints that has plagued Escape From Tarkov, especially after the 1.0 launch, was loading times. When playing online, loading the map and assets and actually connecting to a server were done in tandem. The practical outcome was that you'd often spend 5, sometimes even 10 minutes or more staring at a screen.

Escape From Tarkov developer Nikita Buyanov reveals details about BSG's next game.

Starting with patch 1.3.5.0, Escape From Tarkov now does the asset buffering and server matchmaking in parallel, shaving some precious minutes off of the loading screen.

To help longer playing sessions feel smoother, the game now cleans up after itself better at the end of each raid. This will have a particularly tangible impact for users who aren't hogging up 32GB of RAM instead of sharing it with poor Sam Altman. On top of that, the issues where uncontrolled RAM usage could happen during long gaming sessions have finally been fixed.

Game server performance has also undergone an optimization pass. The practical implication here is that you'll have to deal with less hitreg and packet loss issues. Besides ghost shots, doors will now work properly, removing certain errors where they collide with the player in a jumbled case between the client and server

As part of the new 1.3.5.0 patch, the game has unified its graphics rendering engine under RenderStack. Most of the big improvements from this change are yet to come, but RenderStack lays the groundwork for the future of the game while already giving players some performance bonuses.

Vegetation and long-distance rendering have a new distant projection system, resulting in better graphics for trees, bushes, and other parts of nature while you do your run. This is especially noticeable in the Shoreline and Woods maps, where you spend most of your time breathing in the crisp forest air. Seasonal transitions will now work with preloading landscape materials to significantly reduce RAM usage.

Lighting and shadow transitions will now be smoother, resulting in less strain on the CPU and GPU while the game is running. When staring down magnifying optics, you have fewer frame drops and a crisper image, especially when running upscalers like DLSS or FSR.

In the future, the change to RenderStack will allow Tarkov to use DLSS Frame Generation and FSR 4.0.

It will allow Tarkov to use NVIDIA DLSS technology and FSR 2 and FSR 3

If a player happens to lose connection during a raid due to network issues, it will now be easier and faster to join back up. With the new addition, the game won’t need to reload the entire map, resources, or world state, as it will only require the connection to come back, and you’ll be joined back up with everything else stored where it was left off.

These changes won’t be implemented when the game client closes unexpectedly, such as OS failure, PC restart, and similar changes.

To celebrate, Escape From Tarkov is holding discounts on cosmetic packs in the Expansion Hub of the game for each of the factions, such as the USEC Veteran Pack, BEAR Veteran Pack, PMC Veteran Pack, and an Executive PMC Pack.

Escape from Tarkov is available for Windows via Steam and the official Escape from Tarkov website.

#4086. Heartopia shows off My Little Pony collaboration, and there's a pre-launch event to hold you over

Heartopia’s My Little Pony collaboration is close, and the pre-launch event has already kicked off.

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

If any of that sounds interesting, definitely log in now to play the pre-launch event, which should hold you over until the proper show kicks off Saturday. If you’re already enjoying Heartopia, you likely want to learn about Onsen Egg Promise locations, Fish locations, and Bug locations - all of which can be found at those links.

#4084. GTA 6: Where to Find Cave Diving

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

​There feels like endless activities to do in Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether it’s racing through the streets of Vice City, playing mini-golf with your loved one or robbing banks, there’s no shortage of things to do in this vast open world adventure.

Most of the side activities are hidden, not properly introduced or shown on the map where to find them, and that’s exactly the case for cave diving. This dangerous and claustrophobic activity might not be for everyone, but it certainly can yield you some good rewards if you decide to bring Jason or Lucia down.

Find out how to identify enterable houses on the GTA 6 map, why some are mission-only, and what you can discover inside.

The cave system isn’t too far off from where you start in chapter 2 of the story. You will be able to access it in the first chapter, but it will be a bit of a drive. This is located all the way in Kelly County. This can be found in the western portion of the map.

The best way to find where you’re going is right in-between the L and E on the Leonida text if you zoom all the way out on the map. You will see a rather large network of swamps and rivers called the Emerald Springs. Here, you will want to go directly west of the “Emerald Springs” text on the map, around the rivers and on the western side.

There will be a small hut area on the map that branches off from the road, and this will lead to Selkie Hole. The Selkie is a mythological creature from Norse and Celtic lore. Up here, you will spot various divers and a couple of them just leave their scuba gear out there. Grab them (they won’t care) and head inside the cave through the chain-link door. Down the stairs is the cave system. Happy exploring!

A light illuminates rocks in a dark underwater cave, with an Explorer’s Knife prompt on screen.

Sadly, most of the cave system is already mapped – literally. You’ll be able to open up your in-game map and see just how far the tunnels go, and that’s all there is. Now, we say “that’s all there is”, but in reality, it’s a surprisingly lengthy and sprawling system that will take quite a bit to fully explore.

Because of that, there will be some hidden items spread throughout. One of the most common items in this cave system is Meteorites. These are unique items spread throughout the open world in which you’ll be able to pawn for some extra cash, usually for quite a bit (especially early on). It’s the same as collectibles such as cards and doubloons, but yielding the most trade value.

On top of that, you will find other unique items such as an Explorer’s Knife pretty close to the entrance of the cave system. It’s nothing too special but one that you will always have considering it’s a legendary weapon.

People seemingly haven't been able to stop playing Nioh 3 since the moment it came out, and everyone helped push the numbers to unprecedented heights for the series.

Nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

That’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

#4080. Exoprimal, Capcom’s Anti-Dinosaur Future Shooter, Announces End of Service

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

Live service games have it rough in the current gaming industry, forced to fight tooth and nail against half a dozen well-established titles that have all but consumed the worthwhile player base. Anyone new on the block needs to really justify their airtime, and for many, it’s simply not worth the hassle of getting torn apart by consumers.

Find the Near Fatal Sex Scandal encounter in GTA 6, follow the woman to the estate, and learn how to complete it and earn $10,000.

Some, like Capcom’s Exoprimal, try to throw everything at the wall to see what sticks with players, and I can’t lie, mech suits vs dinosaurs was a compelling first pitch. After three solid years of support, however, Exoprimal is facing End of Service, just announced by Capcom.

Marked for death after September 2027, players have less than a year to enjoy their Jurassic jungle gym.

Exoprimal was an odd title, announced back in 2022 and released in July of 2023. One of Capcom's few big-budget standalone titles, surrounded by its long-running franchises, Exoprimal was Capcom’s attempt to leap into the third-person shooter live-service genre dominated by Warframe.

Exoprimal itself found a niche audience that enjoyed what was on offer, with a humble but positive review on Steam to this day. Despite the receptive crowd, players were disappointed by the lack of content on launch, leaving them with plenty of hunger for more dino-killing, mech-fueled action.

Capcom eventually relented in a series of effective but spaced-out patches, leaving players feeling like the second fiddle as the company continued to focus on its heavy hitters. The End of Service announcement is a genuine death sentence for a title like Exoprimal, not just revealing an end to active development, but a date the game will be simply unplayable after.

The announcement is unfortunate, but sadly not at all unexpected. When compared to other middling live service ventures, Exoprimal managing a total of 4 years of support is on the higher end. This, sadly, just means players who put in the time are left in the dust, at least until they find a third-party way to keep playing.

Anyone new on the block needs to really justify their airtime, and for many, it’s simply not worth the hassle of getting torn apart by consumers

Modders have been the absolute team players when it comes to keeping the lights on for live service communities, and Exoprimal is no different. If they can’t, Exoprimal is facing downright elimination, a sad sight for one of Capcom’s most video-gamey new titles that could absolutely have made it in the long haul.

End-of-Service announcements have killed tons of games, both strong and weak. It’s been a major hit to the industry, with half of the recent releases that drop threatened by an eventual death knell. Any investment in a title that isn’t guaranteed to succeed, like massive franchise sequels, feels like a gamble, and it can be absolutely exhausting.

Capcom is one company that can absolutely afford to put out smaller, standalone titles to make some cash and potentially introduce whole new franchises. Pragmata is one such gem, a fantastic little puzzle shooter that came out of nowhere. A perfect little bite-sized adventure is perfectly Capcom, and their care for anything other than Monster Hunter shows they just truly aren’t great with long-term support.

Compared to Monster Hunter, with its constant new hunts, events, and short-term content to keep players engaged over time, all the while hyping a massive expansion just over the horizon. Exoprimal struggled to offer anything beyond cosmetics and microtransactions for short-term content between missions, making it clear the small team working on the title didn’t get much focus.

Sadly, Exoprimal’s cancellation isn't surprising, but the fanbase isn’t going anywhere. They may be small, but they’ve got the passion and effort to try and keep the party going, at least for a while longer.

#4078. Fishing Inc is Snapbreak's newest release for the fishing fanatics out there, now on iOS and Android

Need to cast your reel? Don't have a fishing spot nearby? Well, then you're in luck because developer Snapbreak have just released their latest mobile game, and this time it's BigBonk Studios and their exciting new incremental fishing game, Fishing Inc, that's out now on iOS and Android!

In Fishing Inc, you, well, fish. No surprises there. But what sets it apart is the depth of content here, letting you fish for a huge variety of species with their own distinct behaviour, including legendary catches, all while travelling to different locations from small fishing holes to the vast blue ocean. You'll also have access to upgrades as you work your way up to bigger and better catches all across the world!

And, to be honest, Reber may not have been far off. Fishing games have always been popular, combining the excitement of increasingly bigger catches while also being surprisingly laid-back. While Fishing Inc is a little more on the fast-paced side, it still doesn't ask more of you as a player than simply casting your reel and bringing in big fish.

Coming packed with a huge variety of species to catch, locations to visit and plenty of upgrades to hunt, Fishing Inc looks to be a perfect new addition to the catalogue of any fishing enthusiast on mobile!

In the meantime though, if you're looking for even more games to add to your backlog, then you've come to the right place. Just take a look at our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) to see some of our choice picks that have launched over the last year!

#4077. Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

After dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

During my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the plan or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for new ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”

The player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”

It feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

Luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

One example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from big crime stories or not?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”

Sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

There’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”

In its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

When we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we said we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, showed that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”

The game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”

#4076. Love and Deepspace ushers in the Year of the Horse with a Wuxia-inspired AU multi-banner and a restaurant management mini-game

A new Love and Deepspace banner event is here with a lot of rewards to earn, and brand-new Memories for all five lads to unlock.

Love and Deepspace has kicked off the next big in-game moment and is celebrating Chinese New Year with the arrival of a new 5-Star Memory Series. This year's spring-themed banner is available now until February 27, and it comes with a host of events.

The Mortality’s Tenderness banner features five new limited-time 5-Star Memories, one each for the game’s five love interests. The theme is all about warmth, reunion, and intimacy, taking place in a Wuxia-inspired setting that's once again an alternate universe from the main story of the game.

The new memory cards are Xavier: Blades with Blossoms, Zayne: Entwined Kites, Rafayel: Carved Gemheart, Sylus: Shared Lanterns, and Caleb: Clearday Return. You can pick three of the five to focus on and further pick one to guarantee on your second 5-star pull; and you can earn wish rewards by making cumulative wishes over the course of the event.

Some of the rewards you could get include limited headwear, Limited Deepspace Wishes, and — of course — Memory-themed outfits and hairstyles inspired by the new Memories. Outside of wish rewards, the Memory Series comes with growth tasks that rewards you with in-game materials for levelling up the new cards during the event. When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

Illusio returns as part of the new event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

There’s a new mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

Furthermore, if you log in for 10 days throughout the event, you can unlock a new outfit set, Wealth Overflow, which can be worn by any of the love interests as well as the heroine. There are other login rewards, too, like 10 Deepspace Wishes, 10 Empyrean Wishes, His and My Outfit sets, two dynamic portrait photo poses, and loads more.

Finally, the Golden Fortune event adds even more daily log in rewards in the form of one free "shake" per day, from which you can earn a random reward of between 68 and 108 Diamonds — that adds up to a total of 1,296 Diamonds if you show up every day.

#4075. GTA 6: How to Buy a Bikini for Lucia

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

So let’s cut right to the chase here: you’ve been obsessively playing GTA VI over the weekend, and now that you’ve had proper time to check out everything on the serving platter here, it’s time you delved deeper into the advanced mechanics or elements it offers, one of which is character customization.

Find GTA 6 Ultimate Edition vehicles, weapons, clothing, and hairstyles, and learn which chapters and locations unlock each item.

Well, if you’re a dress-up or Virtual Photography fan like me, you’re probably trying to hunt every piece of clothing you can for Lucia and Jason. But for today’s discussion, we’re mainly sticking to everyone’s favorite Latina recently, because I’ve seen people trying to put together a good fashion set for her, especially with layering.

And you guessed it, the most essential part of that layering process is… her bikini underwear. I won’t judge what you need that piece of clothing for, so without further ado, this brief guide breaks down where you can find bikini clothing items for Lucia in Grand Theft Auto 6.

The exact clothing store where you can easily buy a Bikini set for Lucia is the De’Luge Swimwear shop located in the east-central part of Vice Beach. There are no restrictions on when you go there, but I'd suggest waiting until at least Chapter 3, since that’s when Vice City officially becomes available. Also, by then, you'll have enough extra funds to splurge on clothing items.

The De’Luge Swimwear shop sells a bunch of high-end clothing items for both main characters, but the notable items are definitely for Lucia, including bikini tops and bottoms, as well as one-piece bodysuits you can layer pants over for a sophisticated look. Besides regular bikinis, the shop also has variations in stock, along with full-body dresses, all of which you can easily access on the upper floor.

Now, here's where things get a little more interesting for those who enjoy experimenting with Lucia's wardrobe.

Unlike some other clothing options in GTA 6, bikinis are sold as separate pieces, so you don't have to stick with a matching top and bottom. When browsing the available designs, you can press R1 on PlayStation or RB on Xbox to switch between the two categories and see what other options are available.

You can purchase individual pieces rather than buying an entire matching set, and once you've bought them, they'll be available in her wardrobe at a safehouse. So this pretty much gives you a little more freedom to put together your desired outfit combinations, especially if you're trying to create a particular style for Lucia, as I've demonstrated above with the Bikini Bottom under her pants.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

#4074. Escape the Baby Alarm is a humorous, heartfelt game about young motherhood, out now

Let's be honest, most of us aren't prepared for parenthood. I find myself constantly shocked and surprised at how many of my peers have already started families, as the idea utterly terrifies me. But if anything gives an honest, heartwarming, humorous look into the experience, it's Escape the Baby Alarm.

This hand-drawn puzzler from Danish developer Julie Normann Bjørnskov boasts a fully illustrated look also created by Bjørnskov. Charting the experiences of a young mother, it fuses puzzle gameplay with comedic interludes as the surreal, stressful nature of raising a child takes hold. Boasting 17 chapters and 38 puzzles, there's plenty there to explore in Escape the Baby Alarm.

It's a concept that certainly sat well with Jupiter, earning Escape the Baby Alarm a glowing gold review. And while those of us still clinging to our youth may find it a bit too real, it's a refreshing take for the many young parents out there.

If nothing else, Escape the Baby Alarm is also proof that on mobile a small indie title with hand-drawn illustrations can still really make an impact on players. So, if you're interested, give it a go with our recommendation!

Speaking of brutally honest reviews, though, why not dive into something more general, like therapy? And you can do so with a gothic twist by trying out Vampire Therapist, the indie visual novel that's just landed on iOS and Android!

#4073. Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

I admire the cozy sim genre. Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own. In an odd way, I find the genre stressful, arguably the opposite of its intended purpose. I will happily and cathartically guide Grace Ashcroft through the tense hallways of Rhodes Hill in Resident Evil Requiem, but Pokémon Pokopia’s seemingly endless list of to-dos makes me sweat. It’s just not my genre, and I have come to terms with that.

Grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics. Bird (and animal) watching, for example, is apparent and encouraged early in the experience. You can also fix up your somewhat dilapidated home from almost the moment you are let loose outside of the opening tutorial missions.

And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.

I climbed to the roof to fix the leak and replaced all the stairs leading up to the home before I ever participated in the game’s namesake and stole a car. Normally, it’s the kind of interaction I skip or choose not to engage with, given the option. Or, I do the bare minimum to progress. Sure, I have all the options in the world to build and decorate a house and make it my own, but… that feels like a lot of work. And I am not an artist.

The “cozy” elements of Grand Theft Auto VI are admittedly different from those in a game like Pokopia or Animal Crossing. You’re not designing your home (though you can pick a paint color), but it feels similar, and I am trying to figure out why I enjoy it here as opposed to other games. Is it because Jason and Lucia are so instantly believable as human beings that I want their home to be nicer?

After some thought, I think it might just come down to Grand Theft Auto VI’s consistently impressive visual fidelity. Replacing the shingles on the roof, for example, offers a close-up look at Jason’s character model, and you can practically feel the texture of the asphalt while the heat of the sun beats down.

I don’t have confirmation, but it also just feels like someone at Rockstar did exhaustive research on what the process of replacing a roof shingle should look like, even if, I’m sure, it probably doesn’t quite work that way in the real world. Jason makes it look incredibly easy, to the point that it had me questioning if I should be climbing up to my own roof and taking care of some loose shingles myself. And you know what is a lot of fun? Watching someone who is good at something do the thing they’re good at.

I’m now into the driving and shooting part of the game (and enjoying that, too!), but I am shocked at how grateful I was to have the option to stay home and put up drywall.

#4072. Watch Diablo 4 reveal the second class coming with Lord of Hatred here

Diablo 4 will show off its upcoming class in a big anniversary celebration that promises even more reveals.

Blizzard has recently been celebrating its major running games by hosting big livestreams to reveal some major changes, and it’s now Diablo’s turn. The Diablo series is 30 years-old, so this all just ties in nicely with some of the reveals planned for tonight’s showcase.

The Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight is set to kick off today at 2pm PT, 5pm ET, 10pm GMT.

The biggest reason why you might want to tune in is, of course, that a whole chunk of the event will focus on Diablo 4. Blizzard will unveil the second class coming to the game with the Lord of Hatred expansion. The developer, of course, released the first of two classes - Paladin - immediately at the upcoming expansion’s initial reveal back in December.

Lord of Hatred is set to arrive April 28, and there’s even more it’s bringing to the core game that will be shown off during the livestream. Blizzard said we can expect a deeper look at the revamped skill trees, as well as endgame mechanics and features Lord of Hatred is set to introduce.

Beyond Diablo 4 itself, the showcase will feature updates on Diablo Immortal, and even Diablo 2: Resurrected. Blizzard hasn’t been teasing any other announcements, but many still hold out hope for a proper Diablo 1 remaster.

#4069. Grand Theft Auto VI's Auto Drive Is A Beautiful And Free Version Of Hands-Free Travel

Grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

This is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

First, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

Next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

#4068. 10 Games That Will Feel Better To Play After GTA 6

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

If you're like 32.5 million other people around the world, you've probably been dedicating a huge amount of time to GTA 6 lately, and you can't imagine what your life will be like when the experience is over.

All good things must come to an end, and eventually, your time in Leonida will reach a conclusion. However, crossing that frontier doesn't necessarily have to be a bittersweet farewell but rather an opportunity to re-evaluate everything that comes next.

Titles like this one help you appreciate the craft of video game development more than ever, as they fully exploit many of the aspects that make the interactive industry the most special of all those focused on entertainment.

Therefore, if these hypermodern times have already gotten to you and are making you nervous about what will come after Jason and Lucia's story, calm your anxiety by checking out this list of ten games that will feel better to play after GTA 6.

If you're wondering how on earth this list is going to start with one of the games most diametrically opposed to the philosophy of GTA 6, like GRIS, the answer lies precisely in that statement.

After an adventure brimming with stimuli, endless possibilities, lengthy explanations, and violence that ranges from the personal to the systemic, what better way to unwind than with one of the most focused and introspective titles ever conceived?

In just three hours, without a single word and in a straightforward manner, GRIS takes you on a soothing path of reflection, making peace with the circumstances, and reveling in an audiovisual experience that engulfs you to the point of baptizing you with its art.

Without bullets or socioeconomic problems that dictate your relationship with the law, but with platforms, elegance, and a creative intent so distinct that you won't be able to help but fall in love by the time the credits roll on the Sunday afternoon it takes to complete it.

The cliché of "best game ever" versus "best game today" strikes me as both amusing and illogical, but I do believe there's some value in considering The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake in light of GTA 6.

Both titles excel in their focus on player freedom, yet while GTA achieves this within a stunning range of action that opens up numerous possibilities, Ocarina of Time Remake does so in a much more concentrated and whimsical way.

The charm lies not in the immeasurable variety of options, but in the immeasurable creativity of the single alternative they offer for each sequence, demonstrating in the process how the notion of agency has evolved over the last 30 years.

They are two ends of the same spectrum, and experiencing the same sense of enjoyment through discovery in such different ways is what makes them complement each other far better than you might initially imagine.

Having spent its entire existence in the shadow of Rockstar's work, returning to Saints Row 2 now that GTA has taken a 180-degree turn in its approach has become more fitting than ever.

Jason and Lucia face a more realistic, weighty world with consequences, masterfully encouraging restraint and attention to detail, breaking the connection that pitted the two franchises against each other for so long.

Hence, whether you're among those who didn't fully embrace the change in philosophy or those who did, Saints Row 2's humor and arcade style are a perfect fit to reduce the pleasurable cortisol rush produced by GTA 6.

Don't get me wrong: I greatly appreciate Rockstar's courage in going against its own trend, though that doesn't mean I'm not much more eager to play a more relaxed game once I decide to stop wandering around Leonida, postponing saying goodbye.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

After GTA 6, it's quite clear the developer has mastered every imaginable variation of the driving genre, which includes the adrenaline-fueled and spectacular style they employed during the Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition era.

The fact that the vehicles in their latest product had to prioritize accuracy and composure was necessary to fit the rest of the game's structure, yet the primal thrill of getting behind the wheel and flying at 300 kilometers per hour in the most improbable way possible was sacrificed.

Consequently, even considering that the genre as a whole is today much closer to realistic simulation than arcade driving, dusting off your copy of Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition after GTA 6 would be in the instruction manual if GTA 6 had one.

Neither approach is inherently better than the other, evidently, but the desire to truly revel in the speed instead of worrying about the cost of a crash will grow stronger on you with each passing second.

Years go by, and it's incredible how no third-person shooter has understood that they are morally obligated to look to Vanquish to understand how to keep the genre from perpetually stagnating.

Gunfights in GTA 6 are technically impressive and an absolute marvel in terms of action sequences, and yet there isn't a second that goes by that I don't think of Sam Gideon and the thunderous perfection of his combat performance.

Instead of being a turn-based confrontation where both sides take turns behind a wall to exchange bullets, Vanquish is a spiral of destruction that doesn't even stop to reload, presenting a striking contrast to the game we're discussing here.

Would being able to slide at full speed and defeat giant robots in GTA 6 make sense? No. Am I dying to play through Vanquish for the thirtieth time for every occasion I have to stay put in cover? Absolutely.

While this might sound utterly personal, few things please me as much as revisiting a developer's older games after a long time, which brings us to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

Being the franchise's installment I've sunk the most hours into and the reason I love open-world games, it creates an intrinsic incentive for GTA 6 because it allows you to appreciate the passage of time.

Many of the gameplay concepts we enjoy in the franchise today, such as character customization, routines, and minigames, were pioneered by CJ, and taking a step back to appreciate what San Andreas did over 20 years ago is magical.

This recommendation might be harder to justify theoretically because, generally speaking, GTA 6 is a vastly superior version, though the magic of nostalgia is something it won't acquire for another couple of decades, while San Andreas has plenty of that.

This is a brief guide that entails the location of the Fast and Furious green Eclipse in GTA 6.

Rockstar did an exceptional job, like few developers in history, of truly discouraging lethal attacks through a bloody, sensitive, and visceral presentation, though it's ironic that these same qualities are what elevate DOOM Eternal.

Being careful with how you drive or which body parts you shoot is excellent, but I'd be lying if I didn't admit that a part of me misses the raw brutality with which you can manipulate the Doom Guy to commit hellish extermination.

The two titles contrast sharply in both their approach to combat and the ease of movement that enables it, so just thinking about DOOM Eternal's levels, flying all over the place while leaping from execution to execution, makes my mouth water.

Furthermore, being able to shoot an enemy entity in the face with a shotgun without being completely dismayed by my own lack of humanity is a significant bonus, because I do miss being able to disconnect from the consequences of my characters' actions.

GTA 6 is a game of distance, in the sense that its experience focuses heavily on trajectories, the separation between spaces, and the distinct biomes, doing everything Yakuza 0 refuses to do despite also being an open world.

Kamurocho and Sotenbori occupy a tiny fraction of Leonida's map, and there's no vehicle other than your own two feet to traverse them, though this allows you to connect with every back alley and building in a way that no other title has been able to instill in me.

That familiarity and closeness with which Yakuza 0 relates to its inhabitants, locations, and activities is invaluable, and although GTA 6 manages to generate identical emotions, the difference in scale creates an impressive sense of belonging to Kiryu and Majima's journeys.

There are many points of convergence, but the size breaks down the comparison, allowing their divergences to become apparent as the hours pass, thus highlighting the asymmetries that each offers to fans of the genre.

It's clear after just a couple of hours of gameplay that Red Dead Redemption 2 is the primary influence on GTA 6, so we can all agree that we wouldn't be here if it weren't for Red Dead Redemption.

Replacing the noise of neon lights and social media with horses and forests is something Arthur Morgan's game could easily do, but what even the legendary outlaw can't achieve is to also hark back to a time when even design was more contemplative.

Unlike its sequel, Red Dead Redemption is a prototype whose full expression was prevented by technological limitations, resulting in a much quieter, more poetic, and simpler journey, but with the hints of grandeur that its direct and spiritual successor would achieve in 2018 and 2026, respectively.

Therefore, riding back through its empty landscapes, conversing with its few interactive characters, and firing its limited guns is the handbrake for the Pegassi Vitello inside which we find ourselves in GTA 6, letting us breathe fresh air and appreciate the beauty of slower times.

Some players may think they should register a hot new sports car as their starter car. There's actually a better choice. Here's the best starter car to register in GTA VI.

If at any point between 2013 and now you had told me that GTA 6 would be much more like Shenmue than any other video game, I would have thought you needed a psychiatrist, but here we are.

If you're surprised by the attention to detail in drinking a beverage, observing the routines of dozens of NPCs, having to stay fit and healthy, or enjoying complex minigames, let me inform you that Yu Suzuki was already doing it all back in 1999.

While Shenmue is more similar to Yakuza 0 in scale, it also resembles GTA 6 in that both embrace a life simulation design, where walking, talking, playing, interacting, and other such actions aren't driven by the sheer volume of fun but rather by the experience of placing yourself in someone else's shoes.

That talent for immersing you in a reactive, living world that transcends your existence is reserved for the legends, and if you can tolerate the difference in technological advancement and size, Shenmue will easily show you why it feels like a great-great-grandfather of GTA 6.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4067. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

#4065. World of Slime is coming to mobile, offering you cute creature-collecting MMORPG fun

It seems that nowadays creature-collecting has become more popular than ever, no doubt helped by the likes of Palworld really blowing the doors off the concept after Pokémon dominated it for so long. And one of the cutest, lightweight takes has now hit pre-registration on mobile with World of Slime!

World of Slime is, well, exactly as described. This cute top-down MMORPG is best described as a mix of Roco Kingdom with a RuneScape perspective, where you explore a world completing quests and tasks, while capturing cute slime creatures to join your roster.

There's also more straightforward MMORPG combat as you battle it out with huge bosses that stand in your way. It's not exactly World of Warcraft, but World of Slime undoubtedly has plenty in the way of potential. And that small scale makes it a perfect fit for mobile, alongside its adorable cast!

At the same time, it's not been received without controversy, and currently sits at a mixed reception on Steam. Hopefully, that lacklustre reception doesn't translate to a lacking mobile launch. But if you are interested, you can pre-register for World of Slime now on the official site!

#4063. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.
