#4062. 8 Things You Must Do Before Ending Chapter One in GTA 6

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

There is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6. You can deep sea dive for treasure, hang out with friends, complete missions, set up for Lucia, and a lot more. However, some of this absolutely needs to be done before you hit the end of the first chapter.

After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.

Note: It is important to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game. There will also be spoilers ahead about chapter one.

Jason and Lucia have a chance to be madly in love in the beginning of the game. If you prepare for Lucia to get out of prison, work on Jason’s appearance, and focus on how they interact with each other, it will build a solid foundation.

There is a hard reset that comes at the end of the first chapter, and for a while, Lucia will be on her own while Jason recovers. With that being said, it will take a bit of a toll on their relationship.

This means that if you raise it up very high in the beginning, you won’t need to worry about needing to rebuild it as much later in the game, saving you a bit of time later on.

Immediately after setting up your BuckMe account, you are told that you need to start saving money. The first goal in the game is to have a total savings of $5,000 stashed away. This is a pretty easy goal to hit, especially since there are a fair number of money-making opportunities in the first chapter.

You want to make sure that you hit this goal, as when the hard reset comes at the end of the chapter, you will lose everything except what is in your savings account.

As an added bonus, putting money away into your savings account will also raise your relationship, so it is a win-win situation. After you have everything saved up, the rest of your money is stuff you can play with.

Explore the money-making methods covered in this GTA 6 guide, from side activities and selling cars to store robberies and bank heists.

Now that you have saved up the necessary cash for your family savings account, you might have some money burning a hole in your pocket. It is time to go on a bit of a shopping spree.

As I said, you won’t be able to take this money with you into chapter two, so you will want to spend all of it. Buy some clothes, and definitely upgrade your weapons.

There is no point in upgrading your car, as you will lose this after chapter one. Instead, focus on increasing your wardrobe and upgrading your weapons as these will carry over into the next chapter.

There are some missions that you only have access to in the first chapter, and some of them belong to Shirley - Jason’s neighbor. She is a kind lady, and she will occasionally ask you to complete a few tasks.

These consist of getting her some alcohol, and stealing a mobility scooter from a lady nearby. They are fun short missions that you can complete within a few minutes, but they are worth doing because they are quite fun.

Don’t worry about the treasure hunting, as you will be able to come back to it later on. Only certain missions disappear after the first chapter.

A guide to all the story missions in GTA 6 including the chapters and the mission titles.

There’s tons of details in GTA 6, which means that there are a bunch of collectibles that you can find scattered about. Some of these collectibles are books and magazines, and several of them are found around Jason’s house.

Before you end chapter one, you will want to get the books around Jason’s house. These include one in the bedroom, two in the living room, a magazine on the back deck, and one in the shed. Each of these disappears after the first chapter.

Along with this, you will want to grab the sunglasses in Donny’s trailer. You will make your way over there during one of the missions in the first chapter, so you shouldn’t miss out on them, but make sure to pick them up while you have the chance.

If you have been focused on upgrading your weapons, gathering clothes, and putting money into your savings, then you will probably need some extra cash in the first chapter. Instead of searching for treasure, you should instead focus on completing the lost drug missions.

There are four lost drug missions around Key Lento and up to the Grassrivers. These are special missions that end up disappearing after chapter one ends, so you will not have the ability to go back and complete them later on.

Since this is the only time you have access to them, you may as well complete them for the extra cash and spend it on stuff that will help you later in the game.

While I have already established that buying weapons is important because they carry over, it is also important to grab the unique weapons that are obtainable early in the game. There are a couple weapons that you can find around the islands in Key Lento, and they will carry you in later parts of the game.

For instance, the Assassin Pistol can be found on a small dinghy on an island and it is great for completing missions stealthily in later parts of the game, and it has become one of my go-to weapons for staying hidden.

There is also a shotgun that you can find that is quite powerful. It gets outclassed by other unique weapons later on, but it is great to have in chapter two.

One thing that is nice about GTA 6 is that it gives you the option to manually save. This means that you can create save points at key points in the game so that you can return to them later on.

I highly recommend completing what you can in chapter one and then creating a save point right before you go to do the tourist trap mission, as this is the last mission of the chapter, and it is also the point of no return.

If you want to play the game over but don’t want to deal with the slower pacing of the first chapter, you can skip all of that with a save right before the chapter change.

#4059. The Video Games You Should Play This Weekend – November 20, 2026

This is it. We finally made it. Grand Theft Auto VI is here. I have played the game for a number of hours and read Matt Miller's glowing review, which you can read here, and I still don't know if I personally believe the game is actually out. But that just might the lack of sleep from staying up late to play Grand Theft Auto VI.

Many games chose to avoid the blast radius of Rockstar's latest crime caper, but that doesn't mean it's the only game that came out this week and you can find them below. But as is tradition, here are some of our top stories of the week first.

If you’re not aware that GTAVI launched this week, it’s possible that you’ve been living under a rock somewhere. Nonetheless, we’re here to offer the reminder that after more than a decade of waiting for a new installment, Rockstar has this week rolled out its new game. It’s good. Like, really good, and if you’re an adult who plays video games, it should really be a title you make time for.

In my review, I highlighted some of its many positive traits, but as you prepare to dive into its criminal delights over the weekend, one element I’d especially like to point out is its viability as a game to play with your partner. Like an excellent prestige TV crime show, GTAVI is a game that features a rich, dramatic, funny, and well-written story that I genuinely believe has the potential to be a good time for both a player and a viewer, though, admittedly, the person who gets to enjoy running the sticks is probably having the most fun.

However you plan to enjoy it, here’s hoping Grand Theft Auto VI turns out to be worth the wait you’ve likely had for it. For my part, it certainly has been, and I suspect you’ll find it only gets better the deeper into the game you go.

The running joke publisher Devolver Digital has made with this “spectacular remaster of the original remake of the unreleased action-platformer starring the most famous video game mascot of all time” is that it launched the same day as Grand Theft Auto VI. Volvy’s Adventure has been positioned as a tongue-in-cheek competitor to Rockstar’s behemoth, with Devovler even releasing a trailer that is a shot-for-shot parody of GTA VI’s. While I’ve chuckled at these stunts, Volvy’s Adventure isn’t just a joke game. It’s actually pretty fun.

For one, it’s developed by a respectable studio in Doinksoft, the team behind fun indie games like Gato Roboto, Gunbrella, and this year’s Dark Scrolls. Vovly’s Adventure is a 16-bit 2D platformer where players use Volvy’s oversized fist to punch through objects, which, in turn, propels him in the same direction. Thus, platforming is a fast-paced and explosive exercise in soaring fist-first through barriers and enemies, collecting items, and burrowing through certain platforms. The platforming feels pretty good, and it’s backed by a catchy soundtrack; the destruction is satisfying; and the levels are relatively brief, making it easy to plow through.

I wasn’t sure what to expect from Volvy’s Adventure beyond the marketing jokes, but it’s got some sauce. Sitting at the budget price of $5 (and a launch discount of $3.74), it’s a curiosity that’s easy to check out.

Australia Did It, from Rami Ismail and his team at Aesthetician Labs, hit a little snag with its publicized release date. Valve got backed up approving the release of games on its platform and a handful of games were affected. Australia Did It, despite the unexpected delay, is out... and it's good! Here's what Brian Shea wrote in his review: "Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world."

God of War Sons of Sparta is... underwhelming, to be blunt. You can read my review here. The game is a prequel where you play as a young Kratos and go on a 2D Metroid-inspired adventure with your brother, Deimos. If you are interested in getting the full God of War story, there are some interesting narrative and character details in the game, but it has some shortcomings. What's surprising about its re-release this week is that it is now available on PS4. An unexpected "new" platform to say the least.

#4057. GTA 6's Collectible Trading Cards Are Getting A Real-Life Release This December

It's been less than a week since Grand Theft Auto 6 came out, and Rockstar Games has already found another way to get us to spend money on the game. If you've been collecting sports cards while exploring Leonida, you'll soon be able to do the same outside the game. Rockstar has partnered with Panini America to bring these fictional sports trading cards to life, and they'll be out in December 2026.

Download GTA 6's official Leonida map and printable cover art free from Rockstar. Here's where to find them and how the physical poster differs.

This goes beyond your usual video game merchandise featuring the main characters. The cards are based on collectibles that actually exist within GTA 6's world, so you might recognize some of the athletes and teams when you open a pack. And if you're hoping to get your hands on some of the rarer cards, there are even a few that are limited to a single copy each.

Panini America announced its partnership with Rockstar Games on November 24. The officially licensed set is called the GTA VI: Sports Trading Card Collection, and it'll be the first trading card collaboration between the two companies.

If you've ever collected football or basketball cards, chances are you're already familiar with Panini. They're also known for reprinting comics in Europe, and I still have a copy of the X-Men: The Last Stand Annual 2007 published by Panini Books.

What's different this time is that instead of collecting cards featuring actual sports stars, you'll be collecting ones based on athletes from Rockstar's fictional universe. The promotional artwork shows a mixture of illustrated cards and ones featuring character renders, much like those found in the game itself.

The cards will come in boxes containing four packs each. Panini says a box will typically include two Rookie cards, a Retro card, an Illustrated card and four Special Silvers. These are average figures rather than guaranteed contents for every box.

There'll also be different colored variants of the cards, including silver, pink, teal and light blue, along with team-colored parallels. The rarest variants have much smaller print runs. The Legend Bronze cards are numbered out of 49, the numbered Silver variants out of 25, and the Gold variants are one-of-a-kind cards.

Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn’t be surprised if some of the rare cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

Getting your hands on every variant, however, could be quite a challenge. Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn't be surprised if some of the rarer cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

Even if you don't care about the numbered cards, there's some appeal in having the regular ones. GTA's fictional athletes aren't exactly household names like the ones you'd find in Panini's other sports collections, but you can actually go looking for their cards in Leonida while playing the game.

Rockstar has been selling GTA merchandise for years, but this particular collaboration reminds me of the sort of extras that used to come with physical copies of video games. The maps that came with older GTA titles, for instance, were something you could actually use while playing and keep long after you were done with the game.

Ironically, GTA 6's boxed edition doesn't even come with a game disc. So it's nice to see Rockstar making something physical that draws directly from the game rather than simply putting its logo on another piece of merchandise.

Rockstar could've easily gone with a conventional trading card set featuring Jason, Lucia, and other major characters. Instead, it's making replicas of things you might stumble across while taking a break from the story. I'd love to see Rockstar do something similar with other fictional brands from the series, like Sprunk or eCola.

Unfortunately, Panini hasn't announced an exact release date, pricing, or which countries the cards will be available in.

Depending on when the cards go on sale in December, they could make for a pretty good Christmas gift for a GTA fan.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

@Chocobo_Shepherd The industry standard for refresh rate is 30fps, 60fps is what native games are suppose to run at but 30fps is standard for everything including music, movies, slides show, cameras, etc., with gaming taking that into account too, etc. It's similar to how resolution works, 480p is standard, anything below that is low quality or low-res, 720p is high quality and anything over that count as high def a.k.a. HD whereas 1440p or over count as 4K.

Also the higher the refresh rate, the lower they had to tone down the resolution otherwise the games won't be able to perform smoothly meaning you can't have 4K and still expect 120fps. It's just not gonna work, not every clear details will fly in 120fps or even 60fps. This is why to keep the details clear and the game smooth, some bigger games target for 60fps only in either 720p or 1080p. Smaller scale games like indies may target 1080p 60fps but that's only cause there's not many details to interfere with the refresh rate.

#4054. Grand Theft Auto VI Shatters Records, Making $3.79 Billion In 24 Hours As The Biggest Entertainment Launch Ever

Grand Theft Auto VI dropped yesterday to massive success, and while we expected it to do well, hearing the numbers behind the historic launch day is still staggering. According to a statement obtained by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier and IGN, Rockstar has confirmed that the open-world juggernaut made $3.79 billion in 24 hours. This makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time – it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and it's not especially close.

Schreier goes on to confirm that much of that money comes from GTA VI's record-breaking pre-orders. It turns out, there were 32.5 million pre-sales, which is a truly mind-bending number. For context, its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, currently the second best-selling game of all time, sold 11.21 million copies in the first 24 hours – GTAVI nearly triples that figure. In pre-orders alone, the game has become the 30th best-selling game of all time, with more copies sold in the first day than Elden Ring and Super Mario Odyssey have sold, period.

In terms of the dollar amount, GTAVI's $3.79 billion in 24 hours is not just more money than any film has made in its opening weekend; it's more money than any movie has ever made in the box office – even Avengers: Endgame, which currently holds the highest worldwide gross, is still shy of $3 billion after several successful theatrical runs.

Grand Theft Auto VI also set the record on Metacritic for the highest-reviewed game of all time (with an average critic score of 99), and it headlined this week's rollout of the Game Awards 2026 nominees, with more nominations than any other game. We also loved it, and our editor-in-chief Matt Miller scored it a perfect 10.

With the nights closing in and the weather getting cold, you may find it a bit difficult to get in the mood for going out. But Pokémon Go has you covered, with a major new event taking place next month, as Gigantamax Inteleon Max Battle Day kicks off this December!

For the first time in Pokémon Go, you'll have a chance to encounter the Shiny Gigantamax Inteleon on December 5th, between 1400-1700 local time. Fortunately, you won't have much trouble finding Max Battles and trainers to help you out, as Pokémon Go is also debuting new improvements to the map to let you find battles more easily.

And, of course, for $4.99 you can also grab yourself the event-exclusive Timed Research, featuring additional XP and Particles, as well as double XP for the duration.

All in all, it's looking to be a pretty solid event. And don't worry if it's a bit chilly where you are and you can't get out of the house. Because Battle Day will also see a marked increase in the number of Remote Raids you can access, so everyone can get in on the fun!

#4052. Team Cherry Teases New Silksong DLC Info After Months of Silence

Patrick Souza is a writer for DualShockers who has been writing for over 5 years, specializing in JRPGs, roguelikes, and other genres such as MMOs. He previously worked for Prima Games, The Escapist, and The Gamer, and holds a degree in Journalism.

Get ready to return to Pharloom as the previously announced Hollow Knight: Silksong DLC might be closer than you imagined. Team Cherry has just announced a new presentation stream named Cherry Time!, where they’re promising to give us new info on the previously announced expansion for their latest game.

Hollow Knight: Silksong lived up to its hype when it was first released back in 2025, and just like its predecessor, it didn’t take long until a new update was announced. However, in a very Silksong fashion, we barely had any new info on it, aside from its name and a promise to be “coming soon”.

It seems that Team Cherry’s playtesters faced a much tougher Silksong.

This is the first time we’ll be getting an actual update on this expansion, which has only received a single teaser trailer so far. And the Silksong announcement might not be the only thing we’ll be seeing here.

Throughout its social media accounts, Team Cherry has announced their Cherry Time! Livestream, a new presentation they haven’t done before. You can watch it live on November 27, 7 AM PT on their official YouTube channel.

Team Cherry is promising “a bunch of exciting announcements” aside from the already expected info on Sea of Sorrow, the Silksong DLC. This could be either new updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

Aside from the initial trailer released back in 2025, the team has been radio silent about its development. This might actually be a great sign, as you’ll know if you’ve followed anything about Silksong’s development cycle in the past years.

The game was originally conceived as an expansion for the original Hollow Knight, where you could play as the supporting character Hornet. However, the project became too big for its own good, eventually turning into a whole new game in just a few years.

This could be either new updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

However, Team Cherry was adamant about never feeding us any new info, leading fans to think the game was quietly canceled or that it was all a hoax from the start. You’ll certainly remember those frenzied fans typing “SKONG??!!” on every single indie game announcement stream (or any stream, really). Things got out of control at a time.

Imagine the shock when we discovered Team Cherry was just too busy adding new things to the game over the years and had adopted a chronically offline posture. We only got actual info less than a month before the game actually came out. We might be seeing history repeating itself here, but I wouldn’t count on it just yet.

From Axiom Verge to Hollow Knight: Silksong, these are the ten Metroidvanias with the most nominations at The Game Awards.

While we were promised that the waiting wouldn’t be as daunting as it was for the base game (which took 8 years to release after the first title), it seems like Sea of Sorrow might be going through the same development hell cycle.

The recently released physical edition of Silksong for the Nintendo Switch presented the upcoming DLC as a “giant expansion” and made no new notes to the 2026 release window, as shown by Reddit user ArchivistOfSkylands.

For all we know, Team Cherry might be taking their time cooking another huge meal for us once again. It certainly won’t take 8 more years again, but we might not be visiting this new ocean of content this year just yet.

The original Hollow Knight had a total of four free updates, which added tons of content such as new endings, more quests, new bosses, and many boss gauntlets to prove yourself as a real God in Hallownest. Fans have huge expectations for Silksong to get the same treatment, especially when it comes to the latter.

We’ll know more about the current state of this expansion in just a few more days. We got a release date for Silksong similarly, coming almost out of nowhere, so it might be the time. But as we’ve seen lately, devs have been taking extra time to refine their final game, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see that happen here, too.

#4050. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4049. Take-Two's GTA 6 PC Port Crackdown Has Already Taken Down Over 3,000 Repositories

Grand Theft Auto 6 is still a console exclusive, but some fans have already been trying to get it running on PC. Take-Two Interactive has filed a copyright complaint against Leonida, an unofficial port based on the Xbox Series version of the game. It's not just the original project that's been affected: GitHub has taken action against a whopping 3,007 repositories in response to the complaint.

According to a new rumor, Rockstar Games could release the GTA 6 PC port just a few months after the highly anticipated console launch.

Leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer. Unlike some of the fan-made PC ports we've seen for older console games, though, this one was being developed using a build of a game that had only just come out.

In a DMCA notice published on GitHub on November 24, Take-Two's intellectual property enforcement team alleges that Leonida infringes upon the company's copyright and violates Rockstar's terms of service. The notice says an Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

The developers had asked users to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build. The company requested that GitHub take down Leonida and its forks, arguing that the alleged infringement couldn't be addressed without disabling the repositories altogether.

GitHub says it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories. That number includes forks, which are essentially copies of a repository that other GitHub users can work on independently. That doesn't mean there were 3,007 different GTA 6 PC ports in development, though.

An Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

According to PC Gamer, the team appeared to have reached the game's splash screen during a livestream before it crashed. The project's lead developer, NotRexed, subsequently announced their departure, citing the loss of the Discord server as well as the pressure of managing the community alongside school and sports.

Take-Two's takedown hasn't put an end to Leonida, either. According to the same report, others have already tried to pick up where the original developer left off.

It's a familiar situation for those of us who primarily play on PC. GTA 4 came to PC several months after its console debut, while we had to wait more than a year and a half after GTA 5's original launch for its PC version. Even Red Dead Redemption 2 took roughly a year to make its way over.

The difference this time is that a report has suggested GTA 6 could arrive on PC in the first quarter of 2027. If that turns out to be true, the wait would be much shorter than it was for Rockstar's last two major releases. There hasn't been an official announcement confirming that release window, however.

Getting GTA 6 to boot on a PC and getting it to run well enough to play through the entire game are two very different things. Just look at how badly Rockstar handled GTA 4's PC port. Even hardware that far exceeded the game's original system requirements struggled to run it smoothly, and Rockstar never bothered to properly fix it.

Modders have spent years ironing out its performance issues and bugs, and while that's still an ongoing process, I'd argue 2026 has been the best year yet to play GTA 4 on PC. Even if one of these unofficial efforts eventually makes it past the splash screen, there's no telling how well the game will run on a typical gaming PC or whether it'll have major bugs throughout the story.

Hopefully, Rockstar won't keep us in the dark for too long regarding the official PC version. Even an approximate release window would be welcome at this point, especially for anyone holding off on buying a console just to play GTA 6.

#4048. How Long Does It Take To Complete Grand Theft Auto 6?

GTA 6 is finally here, and it's much bigger than any of us could have dreamed. Here's how long to expect it to take over your life.

It's been a very, very long road but Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, bringing with it the most detailed and expansive gameplay, world, and story that the series has ever seen.

Considering how many years we've been waiting for GTA 6 and all of the things that Rockstar managed to keep secret for so long, you're no doubt wondering how big the game is. Let's get into it.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is split into five main story chapters, with a total of 93 story missions to complete. Story missions range from being massive set-piece moments that can take nearly an hour each to shorter scenarios that won't take you that long. Each chapter in the game is about the same length, although Chapter 2 and Chapter 5 are a little less lengthy than the others.

If you're looking to just mainline it to the end of the game (which would be a massive mistake, honestly), then you're probably going to spend a minimum of 50 to 60 hours to see the credits. Of course, those story missions are just the start, as there are tons of side missions, robberies, exploration points, and other objectives for Jason and Lucia to complete.

A more balanced playthrough of Grand Theft Auto 6 where you spend some time exploring the world, saving some money, and taking the time to complete some objectives is going to take upwards of 70 hours. By the time I hit the credits, I was 80 hours in and had only completed 62 percent of the entire game, and that was with a little bit of deadline speediness.

Looking for a complete list for all story missions in GTA 6? We have them here!

That should probably clue you in to the fact that 100 percenting Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to take you a very long while. To do so, you'll need to complete all 100 optional tasks, clear all 39 robbery opportunities and 22 bank jobs, fence $100,000 in narcotics and jewellery, collect all the trading cards, find every meditation spot and flamingo, and oh so much more.

It's such an undertaking, in fact, that it was major news when one player managed to get the Platinum a few days after launch. I can't even imagine how that went down.

Simply put, 100 percenting GTA 6 is a huge undertaking that's going to take you a very long time, which is at least made easier with all the trackers in the Progress menu. I'm nowhere near doing that myself after nearly 100 hours, so I'd easily put an estimate of around 180 to 200 hours (if not more) to 100 percent complete Grand Theft Auto 6.

#4047. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

#4046. Company of Heroes 3: Operation Torch Review

Company of Heroes 3: Operation Torch delivers a replayable North African campaign with strong mission design, despite minor frustrations.

Company of Heroes 3 has come a long way since its 2023 release, slowly making its way to the real-time strategy hall of fame after a rather rough start. And yet, until now, something was missing.

Update 3.0 helped bring the game to its full potential, but mechanical polish only goes so far. Until recently, Company of Heroes 3 was a brilliant strategy game with strong mechanics that lend themselves well to single-player, but this was offset by a lack of quality content you could go through solo.

The dynamic campaign remains the highlight of Company of Heroes 3, but thanks to Operation Torch, the game finally has a scripted, story campaign that’s worth the trouble.

Operation Torch is the first single-player campaign DLC for Company of Heroes 3. It was preceded by the unorthodox yet highly entertaining Final Stand tower defence DLC, but surviving wave after wave of German tanks is no substitute for a touching story.

In that sense, the choice to depict Operation Torch is a poetic one. While American forces were being put through wringer in Pacific islands, the US had yet to launch any major land operations against the Germans and Italians.

Frontier Developments returns to the animal park with Planet Zoo 2.

The North Africa landings sent a green Army against veteran enemies. The Americans turned out to be quite adept at learning on the job, but the lessons there were written in blood. As a DLC, Operation Torch is similar.

Company of Heroes 3 emerges victorious once you see it through, but that success comes on the back of some blunders and failures that I hope are not repeated if or when Relic Entertainment decides another story-driven DLC is due.

The DLC focuses on three American soldiers from the US Army’s 34th Infantry Division, all the way from the landings in Algeria to the crushing of Axis resistance in Tunisia.

As far as individual story beats go, Operation Torch is adequate. Becker, Russo and Flanagan are likeable and quite distinct, and their commentary enhances the missions for the most part. There are some occasional immersion-breaking bits that strike out as silly, just about all of them relating to ‘tutorial’ speech.

For example, in a rather late mission in the campaign, Becker instructs us to defend fuel points because “we need the fuel to build tanks.” Well yes, Colonel, in game we do, but I’m operating under the assumption that these tanks were manufactured in a plant somewhere in Detroit rather than spontaneously spawned through good vibes and virtual resources somewhere in Tunisia.

This is nowhere near as egregious as in the much-maligned Rommel campaign that comes with the base game, but it would have been nice to have the option to disable tutorial-style objectives and commentary for people who are familiar with the game or who are going for a second playthrough.

I need to emphasize repeat playthroughs here because, although Operation Torch is a linear, story-based DLC, it incorporates lessons from other Company of Heroes 3 releases that make it more replayable than other campaigns in a similar vein.

Most missions are fairly open-ended in terms of how you can approach them. This is complemented by a decent degree of customization after each mission depending on how you accomplish both primary and secondary objectives. The Italy campaign had similar choices, but the Operation Torch system is closer to that of the Final Stand DLC.

The effects of the upgrades you pick are rather tangible. For example, early on, I managed to unlock M3 assault halftracks as a command call-in. Despite being rather underwhelming in their basic battle taxi configuration, these can be converted into game-changers.

The Americans turned out to be quite adept at learning on the job, but the lessons there were written in blood.

Many of my missions were saved because I was able to bring in an M3 converted into 75mm gun carriers that provided quick, on-call artillery support to break down defenses. When dug in myself, the M16 variant with the .50 quad-mounts made mince out of Axis infantry, allowing outnumbered defenders to hold out. All of this could have gone differently had I chosen another upgrade perk, which would have had its own advantages.

Final Stand’s influence is particularly felt in those defensive scenarios, where its wave mechanics reach their zenith.

Base game mechanics sometimes make these last stands slightly less dramatic than they could be at first, primarily because, as in real life, liberal application of engineering obstacles and overlapping fields of fire make incoming waves trivial. That false sense of safety comes apart spectacularly once heavier armor rolls in and you learn that Bazookas can’t dent it.

Relic managed to craft missions that reward sound tactics. Generally speaking, if it works in real life, it will work here. There is one exception that deserves its own section, and that’s the abysmal commando raid mission.

When the Operation Torch announcement came about late last month, the commando gameplay was by far the most exciting part. I’ve been counting the days until SAS: Rogue Heroes comes back for its third season, and I was hoping the commando levels would be a good way to make the wait easier. I was sorely mistaken, I’m afraid.

The level where you plant explosive charges is an affront to modern game design, primarily because it is just… Pac-Man. With guns.

You play one lonely commando, and your job is to slip by German patrols to plant demolition charges on 88mm guns. Every time you die (which, in my experience, is a lot), you respawn on the last checkpoint. Besides snipers, taking out any enemy does virtually nothing as they respawn almost immediately as well.

The result is a level that’s both archaic and devoid of meaning. There’s no way to fail the mission, as you just keep sending more and more single commandos into the breech, the Germans reciprocate, and you’re sitting there playing Pac-Man timing patrol movement patterns for a dry 30 minutes.

The mission is a one off, much like the American debacle in the Kasserine Pass in February 1943, but it leaves a mark on what’s otherwise a well-built campaign with strong design and balancing.

Playing Operation Torch and the Italy campaign back-to-back has been great because you get to see how far Allied land operations in the Mediterranean Theater of Operations have come from the shaky landings in Algeria to the assault on Monte Cassino that opened the road to Rome.

It’s nice to see an oft-forgotten part of World War 2 history given the attention it deserves. The British and German versions of the fight for North Africa have been told a million times over, but with a few exceptions (most notably Call of Duty 2: Big Red One), the American African campaign is constantly overshadowed by later exploits in Europe and the Pacific.

Operation Torch also lays out a blueprint for potential future DLCs that focus on telling stories, rather than just adding new units to the same old multiplayer slog. The combined force of this DLC with update 3.0 released earlier this month puts Company of Heroes 3 in the spot it was always meant to occupy since its launch.

Relic made a bold choice in depicting Operation Torch to this degree, and it paid off in spades. Company of Heroes 3 mechanics come alive in a fight that doesn’t get the attention it deserves, in spite of occasional hiccups. The first narrative-driven DLC for the game shows that there’s plenty of untapped potential in it, and it’s left me hoping more of them will come.

#4044. Nioh 3 is, unsurprisingly, the fastest-selling game in the series with over a million units sold

Nioh 3 has taken the Nioh franchise to new heights, delivering its biggest-ever launch.

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”

Deborah Ann Woll, likely best known as Karen Page in Daredevil and Daredevil: Born Again, has just been cast as Laufey in the upcoming live-action God of War series. It's a perfect fit, not just because she's a great actress – Woll already portrays the character in the video games.

The live-action God of War series is currently in production, and after a series of headlines about Kratos, it's refreshing to get some news about his late wife, Faye. Also known as Laufey, she dies right before 2018's God of War (which the show is based on) begins. The game centers on a journey between Kratos and his son to spread Faye's ashes from the highest peak in the realms.

Faye is not present in 2018's God of War, but she appears in God of War Ragnarök in flashback and dream sequences. In this game, she's played by Deborah Ann Woll, an oddly high-profile casting for a relatively minor character. It all made sense earlier this year, however, when we learned Woll will reprise her role as the star of God of War Laufey, which tells Faye's story as she fights through a mythological underworld.

It's a cool piece of news, and it implies that Faye will have more of a presence in the series than in the first game, where she never appears at all. As for what shape that presence takes, we have no idea.

Woll joins the likes of Alastair Duncan, who plays Mimir and will also reprise his role. The two don't really interact in the games, however, so it's unlikely to see them share the screen in the series.

The main news around Prime Video's God of War is about its protagonist. Originally announced as Ryan Hurst, the actor suffered a serious injury on the set of the show and was replaced by Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy, Glass Onion) in August. Other key cast members include Callum Vinson as Atreus, Sonya Walger as Freya, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, and Ed Skrein as Baldur.

#4042. How To Unlock Hurricanes In GTA 6.

Here is how to unlock the hurricane weather storm in GTA 6.

There are a ton of items you can unlock during your playthrough of Grand Theft Auto 6. From unique, legendary weapons to gadgets to vehicles, Rockstar has made it worth exploring the state of Leonida. However, one of the oddest things you can unlock is the hurricane weather event.

Tied to a side quest, if you want hurricanes to start showing up randomly during your GTA 6 playthrough, you'll need to do a bit of legwork. Thankfully, the side quest isn't that difficult, but it will require a little bit of time investment.

In order to unlock hurricanes, you will need to first make your way to North Leonard County. Specifically, we are going to the western side of this region, just below the word "North" on your map. We're looking for an abandoned military compound that is completely fenced in (shown above).

This sniper packs a punch, but you have to go through one of GTA 6's weirdest encounters to get it.

You'll know you're at the right place because there will be a ton of warning and "Keep Out" signs on the road leading up to the gate. Ignore the signs, approach the main gate, and interact with the intercom system on the left. You will be given two dialogue options; select both of them to be told not to come into the compound.

Now, from the gate, head right up the hill towards the shipping containers. Look for a red one that is covering an obvious hole in the ground. Get into the nearby bulldozer and use it to push the container away from the hole. Climb down the ladder and make your way through the sewers until you emerge inside the compound.

Here's where things get interesting, as the ground is absolutely covered in mines. These can be seen as small, dark brown circles with the proximity detector sticking out of the middle (circled above). Getting near one will trigger a rapid beeping, and if you're too close, then it will explode.

Don't worry too much, as the mines themselves don't do a ton of damage. However, they will launch you whenever they detonate, which can send you into more of them. If you have a lot of healing items, you can just sprint through the mines and just tank the damage. Alternatively, use your weapon to shoot the mines, prematurely detonating them.

There will also be drones that try to slam themselves into you. Again, just shooting them a few times will easily dispatch these enemies, and they don't do a lot of damage anyway. Your goal is to reach the large metal bunker on the northwest side of the compound. When you get close, interact with the door to trigger a dialogue exchange.

Meet Freddie, the person in the bunker who is not thrilled that you could easily get past his defenses. Because of this, he will tell you to come back in a few days once he's finished upgrading them. Freddie will then disable the rest of the mines and open the gate so you can leave.

Now all you need to do is wait around 2-3 full days for Freddie to text Jason and Lucia back. Until then, there's nothing else you can do, so go focus on completing other missions or activities first. Once Freddie texts you back, stock up on healing items and Adrenaline before returning to the bunker.

Once you get the text from Freddie, head back to the compound as either Jason or Lucia. This time, when you arrive, don't go to the intercom system, as Freddie has installed a few mines right next to it. Park your car and start heading along the right side of the green fence around his base. I recommend bringing an assault rifle or shotgun, as you'll need to deal with multiple drones at once.

Head towards the northwest corner of the fence and look for a large water tower (shown above). Climb up the first ladder on the tower and then jump over the railing to land on the roof of a building inside Freddie's compound. Just like before, there will be a ton of mines all over the ground. Some of them will be much harder to see this time around, so make sure to listen if the beeping speeds up.

These mines also do a bit more damage, so try to shoot and destroy as many as you can to ensure you don't take any damage. About halfway towards the bunker, Freddie will deploy drones in sets of two. Whenever you hear that the drones are released, stand your ground and shoot them out of the sky.

When you destroy the first wave of drones, advance towards the bunker and stop when the next group arrives. Repeat this process of destroying the drones and running across the minefield until you reach the bunker. Try to open the side door again, only this time you'll be electrocuted and Freddie will emerge from the main doors to gloat.

A cutscene will then play explaining why Freddie is in the middle of nowhere and why he needs you to test the defenses. Once the cutscene ends, you'll get a hurricane warning, and Freddie will give you a chance to leave. Agree to exit his bunker, which prompts him to give you a little over $6,000 in cash. Additionally, you can take Freddie's Benefactor and sell it for $13,000 or register it under your name if you want.

This will also unlock the hurricane weather effect for the rest of your playthrough. Meaning, hurricanes can now randomly take place like other weather events!

#4041. EA Sports FC 27 Adds AI Voice Lines of Late Commentator

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

EA Sports has worked with John Motson’s family to bring his iconic commentary to the hit sports game, EA Sports FC 27, as a digital tribute. If you don’t know the name, you will definitely recognize the voice, even if you aren’t a die-hard football fan.

Motson passed away in February 2023 at the age of 77 and was the main commentator for BBC Sport for 50 years. He commented on over 2,500 games and 20 international tournaments on television and radio during his tenure. Motson starred in the same role for the FIFA video game series as its first commentator from FIFA 1996 to FIFA 2006, and also made an appearance in FIFA 19.

FC 27 is the best thing a Career Mode player could ever wish for, but don't expect an easy transition.

The voice of football will return in EA Sports FC 27 in the next game update for all players to use if they wish to do so.

With permission from Motson’s widow and his son, his voice will return as the first late commentator to appear in the series. According to the BBC, EA paid Motson's family for the rights to use his likeness and recreate his voice, but the company would not disclose the financial terms of the deal.

Fred Motson, the son of John Motson, told the BBC it "means an awful lot" to have his dad's voice in EA Sports FC once again. "I grew up with FIFA," he said. "I always used to tell my parents that I needed the latest console for Christmas because otherwise dad couldn't see how the game worked."

Mat Prior, Senior Game Design Director at EA Sports FC, told the BBC, "There was no way we would have moved forward with this in any way, shape or form if they weren't fully on board."

Motson’s voice will return using a combination of old recording sessions and generative AI. Prior explained that Motson's commentary in EA Sports FC 27 was constructed using old lines he recorded over the years and AI. He said it’s "the only way" to make it happen, since recordings don’t exist of Motson speaking about and mentioning the names of modern players.

However, EA assures that the use of AI to recreate Motson’s voice won’t become commonplace. "It's not there to replace commentators in any way, shape or form... there's certainly no future plans to replace anyone with AI," said Prior.

"From a gaming standpoint, it's something we've used for many years - like machine learning to help drive animation systems and so on and so forth," outlined Prior.

The style of football commentary is unique to each individual, and every fan has their favorites. The little quips, tone, and moments of laughter make the voices feel natural, responsive, and immersive, something AI is unable to replicate.

EA assures that the use of AI to recreate Motson’s voice won’t become commonplace.

John Motson’s tribute arrives in Title Update v1.3.0 on 26 November 2026 as an optional commentary, alongside the existing selection of broadcast teams.

Also on its way with Title Update v1.3.0 is further gameplay tuning based on player feedback, including dribbling balancing adjustments, foul call improvements, and interception recovery tweaks. Moreover, you can expect updates to matchmaking and Amps functionality in The Grounds, along with quality-of-life improvements in Manager and Player Career.

This list looks back over the years of FIFA Ultimate Team (FUT) and breaks down the best cards to grace the pitch.

#4040. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#4038. 10 Hidden Secrets in GTA 6 That You Probably Haven’t Found

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

The Grand Theft Auto 6 map is massive - big enough to fit multiple maps from previous games inside of it. With a map that big, there are bound to be a lot of hidden details. If you’ve been exploring Leonida, you may have found some of them.

However, you probably haven’t discovered many of the hidden secrets this new location has to offer. There are hidden missions and interactions that might blow your mind.

For instance, have you discovered the alien hidden within the bunker? Maybe you haven’t been out to sea yet to find the kraken. There’s plenty to discover in this strange area.

Deep in Pelican Valley, you can find an abandoned research center. This is the strange part; that comes when you are inside. The strange part is that when you step inside, you will get assaulted by a giant crab, which is something straight out of a horror movie.

This is a great easter egg in GTA 6, that connects the game to a movie from the 1980s called Island Claws. In this movie, a scientist breeds giant crabs, and then everything goes completely wrong.

Well, a scientist in GTA 6 tried doing the same thing, and it ended up breeding a giant crab that killed everyone, and now it is coming for you.

Once you have made your way to the Starlet Motel in Kelly County, head northwest. Locate the abandoned car with the flashing lights. From here, follow the path into the woods and you will discover a lady being abducted by a UFO. It is a wild sight.

A few days later, go to sleep as the character you were playing as when you found the UFO. This will trigger a dream sequence where you need to sneak around alien eggs. It also gives you a look at the universe.

The whole dream sequence ends with you inserting a serum into a computer. I don’t want to give too much away, but it gets wild and there are cows involved.

There is a strange case that takes you to an alternate dimension in GTA 6. In reality, it seems more like it makes you trip extremely hard, but either way it is out of this world. It all starts by going to a construction site in Millport.

Inside one of the shipping containers here, you will find a mysterious case that you can interact with, though the name of the item is listed as “???.”

From here, get ready to be sent on a wild trip where you need to do a lot of parkour. You basically walk through various shipping containers and reach an area where you must parkour your way to victory. It isn’t just parkour, as you will need to swim at certain points, but it is a trip you won’t forget.

Even with the many easter eggs in GTA 6, you wouldn't expect time travel to be one of them. But you can do it if you're persistent enough to follow a meticulously planned order of steps.

After you have completed the alien abduction event and had one of the weirdest dreams of your life, it is time to rescue an alien from an underground bunker. Once the dream sequence is done, head to Mariana County, just south of Hamlet.

Here, you can find an old secret base. You will need to break in and climb down the ladder to get inside. Type in the code, access the building, and follow the corridors like you did in your dream.

You will need to put in sequences and everything, but in the end, you will be rewarded by seeing a real alien, and you can even help it escape the base so that it can return home.

You may have spotted Skunkape during one of the earlier missions in GTA 6. During your time in Grassrivers, you can spot a creature running across the road. If you choose to follow it, it will disappear, and you may be wondering where it went.

Well, if you continue your search, you can find effigies that look similar to Bigfoot, but this is not Bigfoot. It is another creature known as Skunkape. When you turn away from the effigy, you will get hit from behind, and a cutscene will play.

After you have this encounter, you can go to Skeeter’s Bar in Hamlet and begin a mission for someone who is looking for the Skunkape. It is something you definitely don’t want to miss.

In Grand Theft Auto 5, you could get stuck out in the ocean, and it would require you to swim for a long time to get back to shore. It was very inconvenient, and so players probably aren’t very interested in getting stuck out at sea in GTA 6.

Well, if you decide to go far out into the ocean and wait for a while, you will get rescued by a dog that is driving a jet ski. It is quite odd, but an amazing interaction that you can certainly miss if you never go out of your way to be stranded in the ocean.

The dog will also bring you to an island where there are other dogs, and it will also dig up some treasure for you. At least you don’t go home empty handed for all this work.

You can go searching for treasure in many different locations around Leonida. One of the best places is deep in the ocean, as you can find gold doubloons and more. However, there are some treasures around the map that come straight from space.

If you search around Mount Kalaga, you can find what appears as purple mist. This is an impact crater, and it is one of the few sites where you can find a meteorite that has crashed into the ground.

While a space rock is cool, the best part about it is that you can sell it for a fair amount of money, so you will want to keep it on your person and take it to a pawn shop to get rid of it.

Something that the game doesn’t tell you is that there are cocaine flamingos, which is a term I never thought I would write, but welcome to GTA 6. There are 125 cocaine flamingos scattered around Leonida, and you need at least 100 of them to complete a task.

You can go the entire game without realizing these statues exist, but if you pay attention, you will notice that these lawn ornaments are different from the standard ones found in many lawns.

Instead of having the standard black and yellow beak, cocaine flamingos have a black and white beak. These flamingo ornaments can be destroyed to find bricks of cocaine that you can sell to a dealer.

There are many different strange finds that you can discover under the surface of the ocean. Treasures galore wait for you in the deep, but so do monsters. Thankfully, they aren’t alive, unless you count a shark as a monster.

To the southeast of Gloriana Key, you can find a shipwreck. However, this is no ordinary shipwreck, as it was destroyed by none other than the mythical beast known as The Kraken.

The Kraken’s tentacles are wrapped all around the ship, which reminds me of Pirates of the Caribbean. Keep in mind that you need to swim very deep to find this hidden secret, and it may take a while to spot thanks to how dark the ocean can be.

Find the Kraken easter egg in GTA 6 with this location guide, including where to dive in Vice City and how to get scuba gear.

There is a hotel that is run by The Kingfishers in GTA 6, but they unfortunately aren’t having a great day. This hotel is located in Pelican Bay, and you want to be careful when you go here, as there is a tiger.

When you approach the hotel room, you will hear gunshots. If you make your way over to the area, you will see a massacre, as a tiger is loose around the area and is eating the various gang members.

It is a crazy interaction that is never marked on your map until you are nearby, so make sure you search the entirety of Pelican Bay and don’t miss anything.

#4037. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4035. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4034. The First GTA 6 DLC is Now Live for All Players

If you missed out on the Grand Theft Auto 6 pre-order bonuses, Rockstar is now offering the Vintage Vice City Pack as a standalone purchase. It's available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The DLC, which includes a classic car, a garage and some particularly nostalgic outfits, costs $4.99 in the US on both consoles.

Download GTA 6's official Leonida map and printable cover art free from Rockstar. Here's where to find them and how the physical poster differs.

According to Rockstar's original pre-order announcement, the pack was included with pre-orders of both editions of GTA 6, as well as digital purchases made before November 20. That meant you could still get the bonus if you bought the game on launch day. If you picked up your copy over the weekend instead, you'll have to pay for the extra content.

According to the official Xbox Store listing, the Vintage Vice City Pack went on sale as a separate add-on on November 20. It isn't a story expansion, but it does offer a little more than just cosmetic items for Jason and Lucia.

The most useful part of the pack is arguably the garage. It's located at Shore Court, near Ocean Beach, and comes with a weapon locker and storage space for goods you've stolen and intend to sell to a fence. You also get a 1955 Vapid Stanier, a classic sedan to keep in the garage. The extra garage alone might make the pack worthwhile if you like collecting cars in GTA.

The extra garage alone might make the pack worthwhile if you like collecting cars in GTA.

As for the cosmetic items, Jason gets a pastel linen suit and a retro haircut, while Lucia gets a short red sequin dress and curly hair. There's also a tropical weapon skin that you can apply to most firearms. The design is based on Tommy Vercetti's unmistakable Hawaiian shirt from GTA Vice City, which is a nice little detail for those of us who grew up playing that game.

The funny thing is that you can already unlock Tommy's original shirt in GTA 6 without buying anything extra. The catch is that it involves a rather elaborate Easter egg, so you might want to set aside some time for that one.

Before spending another five dollars on GTA 6, it's worth checking whether you already own the pack. The outfits, vehicle and garage don't all become available the moment you start the game. You'll have to reach certain points in Jason and Lucia's story before you can claim them.

Rockstar published a support article on November 24 explaining how to access the pre-order rewards. Bring up the pause menu, head to the Store section and find the Vintage Vice City Pack. Selecting an individual reward will tell you what you need to do to unlock it, so you don't have to guess which chapter you should be in. Once you've met the requirements, you'll have to return to the game itself to claim the reward. The Store menu tells you how to get it rather than handing you the items directly.

You don't need the Ultimate Edition to use the Vintage Vice City Pack, either. If you bought the Standard Edition on launch day, for instance, you should check your existing rewards rather than assume the pack is exclusive to the more expensive edition. It's sold separately from the Ultimate Edition Upgrade, and the latter has its own selection of unlockable vehicles, clothing and weapons.

GTA 4 gave us two excellent single-player expansions in The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, and we never got anything comparable for GTA 5 despite its ridiculously long lifespan.

Hopefully, Rockstar has something more substantial planned for GTA 6's single-player DLC. As much as I appreciate the nods to Vice City, I'd love to see the series return to the kind of expansions we got with GTA 4.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4033. Mini Review: KuloNiku: Bowl Up! (Switch 2) - A Satisfying, Tactile Cooking Sim

I have a real soft spot for games that simulate cooking. A strange thing given my aversion to crafting mechanics, but cooking? I could do that all day.

KuloNiku: Bowl Up! Is right up my alley, then. Developed by Gamebir Studio, it sees you take on the role of a new meatball restaurant owner. Your job is to pay close attention to your customers’ orders to ensure maximum satisfaction, thus increasing your reputation and revenue.

Your workstation is separated into sections, and you’ll need to tab between them to complete your order quickly and accurately. Someone orders a Classic Bowl with extra chilli? You’ll need to grab your bowl, go straight to the cooking pan, add three meatballs and one noodle nest, then tab over to the chopping board, grab your chilli and finely slice it. Once that’s added, tab back to your pan, chuck the meatballs and noodles into your bowl, add a ladle of broth, then go to your seasoning station. Add a blob of sweet soy sauce and your cutlery, then serve.

If you nail your customer’s order, they’ll shower you with praise and chuck a few coins into your tip jar. Get something wrong and they’ll let you know, but there generally isn’t any major penalty. If you really mess up, your customer may ask for a full refund, lowering your reputation.

As you complete orders and memorise your recipes, you’ll complete tasks a lot faster. It’s such a tactile experience, too. Using an on-screen cursor, you have to manually select each ingredient while having direct control over your knife when slicing through veg. It serves as the perfect game for mouse controls on Switch 2, giving accuracy that feels otherwise limited via analogue controls. In handheld, the touchscreen can be used to cycle through dialogue but not for cooking.

In addition to cooking, you can decorate your restaurant, visit the shop to purchase new ingredients and items, and nurture your relationships with NPCs during your time off. This usually involves visiting new areas of the neighbourhood and engaging in dialogue. Each area is a static background, so don’t go expecting to wander around; the focus will remain on your conversations.

Finally, you have Meatball Brawls, or ‘Meatbrawls’. These are scheduled competitions in which you showcase your cooking skills to be judged against an opponent. You’ll need to be on your toes with this, as the judges and audience throw in fresh requests in the heat of battle, forcing you to reconsider your flow to accommodate new ingredients. Win the brawl, and you’ll gain an even stronger reputation.

Overall, I found all of the activities outside of the kitchen to be fun enough, but I was constantly eager to get back to cooking. If the game is missing a key ingredient, it’s a mode in which you just cook recipes over and over. The main campaign limits you to just three customers per in-game day, which is a shame. Otherwise, it’s a great time for budding restaurateurs.
